clue.text: A largely aggravated mannerism provides a puzzle

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is kept, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: aggravated, in the sense of annoyed, means cross
a tic is a habitual twitch or mannerism

explanation.surface: Someone's irritating habit is so annoying it becomes a riddle in itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims the last S from CROSS, leaving CROS.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of puzzle hides a word in the initial letters of successive lines.

clue.text: A petal at first concealed plant pest

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word petal

parts.note: concealed means hid

explanation.surface: A gardener finds a pest lurking behind a flower petal.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: Diffusing energy in sex-appeal — a help when turning up in music party

indicators.note: in places the reversed letters inside the word for the party

parts.note: a rave is a large dance-music party

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal, as in the film It
a help is an aid

explanation.surface: Someone's charisma gives them a helping hand when they appear at a dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex-appeal' as IT is an old convention from the 1927 Clara Bow film It; 'when turning up' reads upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emitting energy outward as rays or waves, such as heat, is described this way in physics.

clue.text: Insect infesting secluded hut

indicators.note: infesting means the insect gets inside the other word

parts.note: secluded, keeping out of company, can mean shy
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Bugs have overrun a remote little cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude makeshift dwelling, a shack.

clue.text: Vice unit working to apprehend Duke following certain reasoning

indicators.note: to apprehend means to catch and hold, so the letter goes inside
working signals the letters of vice unit being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Police vice squad detectives arrest an aristocrat after following a line of logic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges VICE UNIT into INUCTIVE; 'to apprehend' holds D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning from particular instances to general laws is the inductive kind of logic.

clue.text: Remarkable assistance for speaker besetting a Government

indicators.note: besetting means surrounding, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a mic (microphone) helps a speaker be heard

explanation.surface: A government spokesperson gets surprisingly good help with their speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, something wonderful or excellent is called magic.

clue.text: Repair a barrel when in temper

indicators.note: when in places the barrel phrase inside the word for temper

parts.note: temper as a state of mind is a mood
a keg is a small barrel

explanation.surface: Someone in a foul temper fixes a barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To make good is a phrasal verb meaning to fix or put right damage.

clue.text: Openings to pick up collection of cutlery, say (silver)

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a set of cutlery is one example of a set
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect a canteen of silver cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: Gates are openings in a fence or wall that let people through.

clue.text: Chap clutching club in bed is a fighter

indicators.note: in places the club-holding chap inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the club goes inside the chap

parts.note: a chap is a man
a bat is a club, as in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A man sleeping with a cudgel in his bed is clearly spoiling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A combatant is someone engaged in fighting, such as a soldier in a war.

clue.text: A lot of confusion over a weathered landscape feature

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: confusion is a mess

explanation.surface: A messy jumble lying on top of an eroded landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims MESS to MES; 'over' puts it above A in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat-topped hill with steep sides is carved out by erosion, typical of the American Southwest.

clue.text: Man's cry of surprise about academic degree — it involves hunting around

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the academic degree goes inside

parts.note: a man's things are his
a dean is a senior academic
eek is a cry of fright or surprise

explanation.surface: A man squeals with surprise at someone's university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's game has one player searching for the others who have hidden.

clue.text: Corporation mostly not commenting after setback

indicators.note: after a setback the letters run backwards
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: not commenting means staying mute

explanation.surface: A company stays largely silent after a business reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims MUTE to MUT; 'after setback' turns it round. Corporation is a jocular old word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a humorous term for a large belly, and a tum is a stomach.

clue.text: It's brought back in The Return of the King, perhaps — must be radical

indicators.note: in places one reversed part inside the other
return of means the word comes back the other way

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card

indicators.note: brought back means the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A film reviewer says something about Tolkien's The Return of the King being bold.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is a decoy: 'Return of' and 'brought back' are both reversal signals, and the king is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic and radical both describe extreme, far-reaching measures.

clue.text: Major golf venue in well-respected area

parts.note: august means venerable or highly respected

explanation.surface: A prestigious golf course is located in a highly regarded neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masters, one of golf's four majors, is played each year at this Georgia club.

clue.text: Boxer's weakness possibly gets one knocked out of series

indicators.note: knocked out of means removed from the word for series

parts.note: a series of linked things is a chain
a means one

explanation.surface: A boxer's flaw might see him eliminated from a run of fights.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jaw is a boxer's vulnerable spot, so a weak point on the face suits the definition.

clue.text: Cast iron's out of place as a breakfast item

indicators.note: out of place signals the letters of cast iron's being moved around

explanation.surface: A cast-iron pan seems out of place at the breakfast table.
explanation.definitionFit: This flaky crescent-shaped French pastry is a breakfast staple.

clue.text: Fix a drink, father — cocktail?

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it
cola is a soft drink
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad is asked to make up a drink, perhaps a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: This rum, coconut and pineapple concoction is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Article with suggestion: chopped oats for part of meal

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a tip is a hint or suggestion

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters of oats are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece advises chopping oats as part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian starters of cured meats and pickles come as the first course of a meal.

clue.text: In mood, possibly, to tuck into every individual fruit product

indicators.note: to tuck into puts the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: every individual means all of them

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of in mood

explanation.surface: Everyone is in the mood to tuck into some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals the anagram of 'In mood'; 'to tuck into' looks like eating but means insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil pressed from almond kernels, the seed of a stone fruit, is a fruit product.

clue.text: Small-bore weapon identified in translation of Pale Fire

indicators.note: translation of signals the letters of Pale Fire changed into a new form

parts.note: the letters of Pale Fire, a novel by Vladimir Nabokov

explanation.surface: A gun turns up in a translated edition of Nabokov's novel Pale Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, small-calibre gun once used for shooting small game was named for its pea-sized bore.

clue.text: Tires excessively by pushing into gnarled trees

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdo

indicators.note: pushing into means the letter goes inside the rearranged trees
gnarled means twisted, so the letters of trees are twisted round

parts.note: X stands for by, as in 3 x 4

explanation.surface: Someone wears themselves out forcing a way through twisted trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excessively' looks part of the definition but supplies the first four letters; 'by' as X comes from multiplication.
explanation.definitionFit: Exerts in the sense of strains or wears out; tires means drains of energy.

clue.text: Period recalled in broadcast

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a period is a time

explanation.surface: A historical era is remembered in a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out a signal, as a transmitter does.

clue.text: Commission functioned as bridge between queen and daughter

indicators.note: a bridge between two things sits in the middle, so it goes between them

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen's royal cipher
functioned means ran, as a machine runs

explanation.surface: A royal commission linked a queen and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a task one is commissioned to carry out for someone.

clue.text: Small, almost slight, having orange colouring

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: a slight is an insult, an affront

explanation.surface: Something small and barely slight has an orange tint.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is the deep orange-yellow of the spice made from crocus stigmas.

clue.text: Just retaining King's ascetic

indicators.note: retaining means holding within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: just means fair
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A fair-minded monarch keeps a holy man at court.
explanation.definitionFit: A fakir is a Muslim or Hindu holy man living by begging and self-denial.

clue.text: Futile cut in sound thinking

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: futile means of no use

explanation.surface: Pointless spending cuts made in the name of sensible thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes the E off NO USE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is British informal for common sense, practical intelligence.

clue.text: Vegetable available in standard and bargain price

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a snip is British informal for a bargain

explanation.surface: A vegetable on sale at its normal and reduced price.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Quietly blocking agreement being upheld, applying pressure

indicators.note: blocking means getting in the middle of, so the letters go inside
in a down clue, upheld means held upside down, read upwards

parts.note: yup is a casual yes
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone quietly obstructs a deal being ratified, putting on pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upheld' turns the agreement upside down, which in a down clue means reading it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy person is forceful and assertive, always applying pressure.

clue.text: Boat mischief, line being cut

indicators.note: being cut means a letter is removed

parts.note: a lark is a piece of mischief or a prank

explanation.surface: Some mischief on a boat ends when its mooring line is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's ark is the famous boat of the flood story.

clue.text: Soon to be involved with sea and surf for a year?

indicators.note: involved means mixed together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is soon going surfing at the beach for a whole year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be involved' rearranges SOON, SEA and SURF together.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring, summer, autumn and winter together make a year, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A crowd, it's said, about to appear in article

indicators.note: to appear in means the letters go inside

parts.note: the is the definite article
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A crowd is said to be about to feature in a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes this number a crowd.

clue.text: Heading off activity cutting anagrams etc

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is taken away

parts.note: fencing, an activity of cuts and thrusts, is swordplay

explanation.surface: A start to some activity that slashes anagrams and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: Anagrams, puns and hidden words are kinds of verbal games with language.
